clue.text: Suspiciously viewed so tall a story handed down

indicators.note: something done suspiciously is shady and out of order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone eyes a far-fetched yarn with suspicion as it is passed down the generations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suspiciously' shuffles VIEWED SO TALL; the 'a' after them belongs to the definition, not the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Folklore and superstitions passed from generation to generation are traditionally called this.

clue.text: Soldiers' letters regularly revealing poetry

indicators.note: regularly asks for every other letter of the word, here the second, fourth, sixth and eighth

explanation.surface: Letters home from soldiers turn out to be poetic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letters regularly' takes alternate letters of SOLDIERS, starting with the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Odes are lyric poems, so a collection of them is poetry.

clue.text: Twice as many with little time to get the jacket

parts.note: to double something is to have twice as many
T is the short form of time

explanation.surface: Getting twice as many jackets in a short time.
explanation.walkthrough: A doublet is the close-fitting jacket worn by men in Tudor and Elizabethan times.
explanation.definitionFit: A doublet is a historical close-fitting man's jacket.

clue.text: Relaxes with noisy gods

indicators.note: noisy says the word for gods is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: idols are false gods or objects of worship

explanation.surface: Someone takes it easy in the company of loud deities.
explanation.definitionFit: To idle is to laze about doing nothing, a synonym of relaxing.

clue.text: Blow the whistle on former model

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
to model for an artist is to pose

explanation.surface: Exposing the secrets of a one-time fashion model.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean to reveal wrongdoing publicly, as an informant does.

clue.text: Swing — net added to facility, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the pieces are judged by how they sound when spoken

parts.note: a trap is a net for catching, and ease means facility; one after the other they make the spoken word

explanation.surface: A playground swing with a safety net bolted onto the structure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'added to' puts TRAP (net) before EASE (facility), and 'we hear' says TRAP-EASE is said like the circus apparatus.
explanation.definitionFit: A trapeze is a horizontal bar hung on ropes that acrobats swing from.

clue.text: Lots of burdens

explanation.surface: Plenty of loads to carry.
explanation.definitionFit: Loads is casual speech for a great many, and also means heavy weights carried.

clue.text: Witty responses about legal wrongs

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in business letters
torts are civil wrongs in law, such as negligence

explanation.surface: Clever comebacks on the subject of lawsuits.
explanation.definitionFit: A retort is a sharp or witty reply.

clue.text: Some people qualified on level terms

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A few qualified people are regarded as peers.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on level terms means neither side is ahead, which is being even.

clue.text: Calm when calcium's found in bridge

indicators.note: found in puts the calcium symbol inside the word for bridge

parts.note: a dental bridge is a plate carrying false teeth
Ca is the chemical symbol for calcium

explanation.surface: A patient is soothed once calcium turns up in a dental bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: To placate is to pacify or soothe someone who is angry.

clue.text: Ready to blast off — as happens under anarchy?

explanation.surface: A rocket launch countdown, set against a society without government.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes 'go' as 'disappear': under anarchy, every system of order goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Mission control's launch call means everything is ready; under anarchy every system of order would vanish.

clue.text: Vessel carrying a Royal Navy bird

indicators.note: carrying means the vessel holds the other pieces within it

parts.note: a bowl is a vessel for holding food or liquid

explanation.surface: A navy ship transports a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a ship beside 'Royal Navy', but it is a bowl.
explanation.definitionFit: A barn owl is a pale owl that roosts in farm buildings.

clue.text: Wait for a motorcycle race to finish

parts.note: the TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man
the end is the finish

explanation.surface: Spectators wait for a motorbike race to reach its finish.
explanation.walkthrough: Attend in its old sense means to await, so 'Wait for' fits.
explanation.definitionFit: In older English attend meant to await or look out for something.

clue.text: Closest Eastern muddle

indicators.note: a muddle is a jumble, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: The nearest Eastern region is in a mess.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearest is the superlative of near, meaning least distant.

clue.text: Identify investigator I have briefly left

indicators.note: left means departed, so these letters go away from the longer word

parts.note: a detective is a police investigator
I have shortened is the contraction I've

explanation.surface: Picking out a detective after a brief departure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' contracts 'I have' to I'VE, and 'left' takes those letters off the end of DETECTIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To detect is to discover or spot, a synonym of identify.

clue.text: Australian mammal is chained, appallingly

indicators.note: appallingly suggests something badly done, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: An Australian animal is cruelly kept on a chain.
explanation.definitionFit: The echidna is a spiny egg-laying mammal of Australia and New Guinea.

clue.text: An application not available to contain sickness

indicators.note: to contain means the abbreviation for not available wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: taken as written
application means use, as in the application of force

explanation.surface: An app that is unavailable is said to contain a cure for illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Nausea is the feeling of sickness in the stomach.

clue.text: Female panellist on Loose Women

parts.note: a straight general-knowledge description of a presenter on the daytime TV talk show

explanation.surface: A guest on a TV discussion show.
explanation.walkthrough: Loose Women is a British daytime ITV talk show presented by a rotating panel of women; this actress and presenter has been one of them for years.
explanation.definitionFit: The actress and TV cook has long been a regular presenter on that ITV chat programme.

clue.text: Bandit took some of the same again

indicators.note: some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A robber helps himself to a share of the same loot again.
explanation.definitionFit: Ditto is used to repeat what was just said, meaning likewise.

clue.text: Bitter dancer lied regularly

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter, starting from the second

explanation.surface: A resentful dancer was routinely dishonest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the even letters of DANCER LIED: A, C, R, I, D.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrid describes a sharp, harsh taste or smell, so it is a synonym of bitter.

clue.text: Cook is a sore point

explanation.surface: A chef who is a touchy subject.
explanation.definitionFit: Boil is a cooking method in hot water, and also an inflamed pus-filled swelling on the skin.

clue.text: Last in row is sent wrong Observer

indicators.note: Last in takes the final letter of the word that follows
wrong means the letters are put in the wrong order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The last person in a row is sent to the wrong newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Observer' looks like the British Sunday newspaper, but it means an onlooker.
explanation.definitionFit: A witness is someone who sees an event, an onlooker.

clue.text: Travelled with nothing on to Wild West show

parts.note: rode is the past tense of ride, meaning travelled on horseback
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A cowboy rides naked to a frontier show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with ... on to' means the O is attached after RODE.
explanation.definitionFit: A rodeo is a show of cowboy skills such as bronco riding.

clue.text: All out using two brushes?

explanation.surface: Giving everything, with a brush in each hand.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading points to two kinds of brush, one for the mouth and one for the fingertips.
explanation.definitionFit: Fighting this way means with every effort; it also names the two body parts that have their own brushes.
